snippet.title: 5 Walmart CB Radios Everyone Ignores (But They're Absolute GOLDMINES)
snippet.description:
📘 The CB Counter Manual: if you'd rather start with a 1970s set for the same money, chapter 21 (page 22) is how I'd spend a hundred dollars, radio, meter and coax included:
https://cbcountermanual.com

Where the facts come from: prices, sellers and ratings were read off walmart.com product pages on 11 November 2026. They move every day, and the store pickup shown was for the store Walmart matched to my browser, not yours. Manufacturer pages: cobra.com (29 LTD) and uniden.com (PRO520XL, PC68LTXFM). The President Ted's FCC grant (2AEOCPC218, 16 May 2024). The Bearcat 980's specs come from a CB dealer's page, and the Cobra 19 Ultra 6 comparison from a published tester's review. Cobra has no product page for the 19 Ultra 6 that I could find. The rules: 47 CFR 95.967 (4 watts AM/FM, 12 watts PEP single sideband), the FCC's 2021 order allowing FM on CB, and the end of CB licensing in 1983.

For the comments: what's on the CB shelf at your Walmart? The website and the store aren't the same thing. And if you bought one of these five, how is it doing?

I ran the counter of a CB shop in Seymour, Indiana, from 1974 to 2008. I was never the bench man and I'm not an engineer.

snippet.title: Why Did Russian Diesel Tankers Suddenly U-Turn Outside New York?
snippet.description:
In early November 2026, three commercial tankers carrying Russian diesel from the Baltic port of Primorsk stalled across the Atlantic before turning away from the U.S. East Coast, just weeks after the U.S. Treasury signed General License No. 135 authorizing Russian diesel imports through April 7, 2027. Why would the world's largest crude oil producer (~13.9 million barrels per day) ever need Russian diesel for New York — and why did zero barrels reach the pier? Using U.S. Energy Information Administration, Maritime Administration, Treasury, and statutory records, we trace how East Coast refinery closures, a full Colonial Pipeline ending at Linden, New Jersey, the 1920 Jones Act's 56-tanker bottleneck, and Congress's 2022 statutory ban collided at the dock.

HFGCS (High Frequency Global Communications System) is a worldwide military radio network operated by the United States Air Force. It uses high-frequency (HF) shortwave radio to communicate with military aircraft, ships, and ground stations over long distances. The system is especially important for emergency communications, military coordination, and transmitting Emergency Action Messages (EAMs), including those related to nuclear command and control. It can remain useful when satellite or other communication systems are unavailable.

snippet.title: He Activated SOTA in All 45 States — Tom K6TAA
snippet.description:
Tom Armer K6TAA grew up a five minute bicycle ride from a 10,000 foot peak in New Mexico, spent his summers peak bagging and wilderness backpacking, and eventually discovered SOTA. What followed was a years-long mission to activate at least one summit in every state that has a SOTA peak. All 45 of them.

In this episode Tom walks through his journey from his first activation at the Pinnacles in California to 14ers in Colorado, volcanic cores in New Mexico, the high point of Nevada, Mount Marcy in New York, and peaks in Alaska and Washington. We talk gear, antenna rigging on rocky summits with no good ground, battery management in cold weather, and the remarkable community of chasers and activators who made it all possible.

snippet.title: Why Ships Carry Three Different Radios
snippet.description:
On a ship's bridge, one radio reaches a coast station 20 to 30 miles away, another follows the sea for 150 miles, and a third can reach across an entire ocean. 

The difference is not just power — it is the path each radio wave takes around the curve of the Earth. Why does modern maritime navigation rely on three separate radios instead of just one?

In this breakdown, we examine the physics, practical frequencies, and maritime regulations behind bridge communications:

• VHF (156–162 MHz): Waves under 2 meters long traveling in near-straight lines. Why antenna height dictates the horizon limit (20–30 NM to shore, less between ships).
• MF (around 2 MHz): Ground wave propagation. How saltwater conductivity prevents energy loss, why the 137-meter wave of 2182 kHz follows Earth's curvature up to 150 NM, and why it reaches much further after sunset.
• HF / Shortwave (4–26 MHz): Ionospheric skywaves. How free electrons bend radio waves up to 4,000 km per hop across oceans.
• The Skip Zone: Why a ship thousands of kilometers away receives a clear signal, while a station just a few hundred kilometers away hears absolute silence.
• Day vs. Night Frequency Shifts: How the absorbing D-layer (60–90 km) collapses at night, requiring operators to switch from 12–16 MHz by day down to 4, 6, or 8 MHz at night.
• Marconi’s 1902 Atlantic Puzzle: Crossing on the liner Philadelphia and discovering the night propagation mystery (1,100 km day vs. 3,400 km night).
• Solar Flares: How solar X-rays reach Earth in 8 minutes, supercharging the D-layer and causing sudden HF blackouts on the sunlit hemisphere.
• Regulations & Satellites: Why international maritime rules still mandate VHF, MF, and HF based on distance from coastlines, especially where satellite systems lose coverage.

₹100, 5 Weeks, One Exam: Get Your Ham Radio Licence in India.

When the phones die and the internet goes dark, one radio can still get through.

This is a complete beginner's guide to amateur (ham) radio in India: what it is, why it is far more than a hobby, how hams talk through satellites and the International Space Station, and exactly how to get your own licence and call sign.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
- What amateur radio is, and how it connects distant friends without phone or email
- Why it keeps working in cyclones, floods and earthquakes when other networks fail
- How hams use low-Earth-orbit satellites and the ISS repeater
- The two Indian licence grades: Restricted and General
- What to study, in order, in 5 to 8 weeks
- Morse code for the General grade (with audio)
- How to book the ASOC exam on Saral Sanchar, and the fees
- Where exams are held and which clubs help new candidates
- Your first station: what to buy first and what can wait
- Safety, rules and on-air etiquette

snippet.title: How Ferrite Rod Antennas Made Pocket AM Radios Possible Without Long Wire Aerials
snippet.description:
Before pocket radios became possible, AM receivers often depended on long wire antennas, large loop aerials, or bulky cabinets designed around the physical size of radio waves.

The ferrite rod antenna changed that.

By wrapping a coil of fine wire around a high-permeability ferrite core, engineers created a compact internal antenna capable of receiving medium-wave AM broadcasts without a long external aerial. Combined with the transistor, this technology helped make radios such as the Regency TR-1 and early Sony pocket radios truly portable.

This video explores how ferrite rod antennas work, how ferrite materials transformed AM radio design, and why the loopstick antenna became one of the hidden components behind the transistor-radio revolution of the 1950s and 1960s.

You’ll also discover why ferrite rods could not follow radio into the higher frequencies used by FM, how telescopic whip antennas took over those bands, and why digital media eventually pushed AM radio out of the center of consumer electronics.

Yet the ferrite rod never disappeared. Today, the same magnetic principles survive in automotive key fobs, immobilizer systems, RFID technology, industrial tracking, and other low-frequency communication systems where modern high-frequency antennas cannot easily replace them.

snippet.title: У нас то мир будет, но не с Украиной! Россияне о переговорах трёх сторон в Абу-Даби. Опрос
snippet.description:
Трамп после встречи с Дмитриевым анонсировал «большое, прекрасное соглашение» по Украине, которое может затронуть всю Европу

Войну в Украине удастся закончить «довольно скоро», заявил президент США Дональд Трамп журналистам в Белом доме. Будущее соглашение, по его словам, выйдет далеко за рамки одной Украины:

«Будет заключено соглашение, это будет большое соглашение, и оно затронет не только Украину. Я бы даже сказал, что оно может охватить всю Европу. Это будет большое, прекрасное соглашение, и все будут в восторге»

Кто подпишет соглашение и когда, Трамп не сказал. Никаких условий он тоже не раскрыл: ни по территориям, ни по гарантиям безопасности, ни по санкциям, пишет Clash Report.

Незадолго до этого американский президент встретился со спецпосланником Путина, главой РФПИ Кириллом Дмитриевым. О чем шла речь, Трамп рассказывать отказался, передает AFP. С украинскими представителями, которые в тот день тоже были в Белом доме, он не встречался.

Российская и украинская делегации приехали в Вашингтон на встречу с первой леди Меланией Трамп. Встреча была посвящена перемирию в подконтрольных России Алешках (украинское название — Олешки). Через участников она передала личные письма Путину и Зеленскому. Россию в Белом доме представляли Дмитриев и уполномоченная по правам человека Яна Лантратова, хотя оба с 2022 года находятся под американскими санкциями.

Следующий раунд переговоров России, США и Украины, по словам пресс-секретаря Кремля Дмитрия Пескова, пройдет 10–11 ноября в Абу-Даби.

Трамп после встречи с Дмитриевым анонсировал «большое, прекрасное соглашение» по Украине, которое может затронуть всю Европу

Войну в Украине удастся закончить «довольно скоро», заявил президент США Дональд Трамп журналистам в Белом доме. Будущее соглашение, по его словам, выйдет далеко за рамки одной Украины:

«Будет заключено соглашение, это будет большое соглашение, и оно затронет не только Украину. Я бы даже сказал, что оно может охватить всю Европу. Это будет большое, прекрасное соглашение, и все будут в восторге»

Кто подпишет соглашение и когда, Трамп не сказал. Никаких условий он тоже не раскрыл: ни по территориям, ни по гарантиям безопасности, ни по санкциям, пишет Clash Report.

Незадолго до этого американский президент встретился со спецпосланником Путина, главой РФПИ Кириллом Дмитриевым. О чем шла речь, Трамп рассказывать отказался, передает AFP. С украинскими представителями, которые в тот день тоже были в Белом доме, он не встречался.

Следующий раунд переговоров России, США и Украины, по словам пресс-секретаря Кремля Дмитрия Пескова, пройдет 10–11 ноября в Абу-Даби.

snippet.title: The beginner's guide to antenna baluns and RF chokes: What they are and how they work

You'll learn how baluns balance antenna currents, the critical differences between voltage and current designs, and why omitting one can distort your dipole's radiation pattern. We also explore feedline dynamics, why air-core chokes often fall short, and how ferrite toroidal chokes stop stray RF from returning down the outside of your coax.

I put the Junbpaw LGE-3080Ti inverter through real-world power testing, running loads up to 1,000 watts before investigating RF interference and its effects on my Icom IC-705 HF/VHF/UHF transceiver. In this video, we examine the evidence, investigate the symptoms, and explore what happens when off-grid power equipment meets sensitive ham radio electronics.

⚠️Please note that I was unable to perform the spurious emissions test due to not having the appropriate high-power RF attenuator on hand.

snippet.title: UV-5RM GMRS in 4 Easy Steps 📡
snippet.description:
Learn the basics of a UV-5RM GMRS handheld in under a minute.

In the U.S., GMRS requires an FCC license — currently $35, good for 10 years, and it covers your immediate family. No exam.

Step 1: Charge with the radio off (Type-C or the cradle), screw the antenna on clockwise, then twist the top knob to power on and set volume.
Step 2: Press VFO/MR for channel mode, then use the arrow keys or type a 3-digit number to pick a GMRS channel.
Step 3: Hold the side PTT, talk about 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) from the mic, and release to listen. Red LED = transmitting. Green LED = a call coming in.
Step 4: Privacy tones like CTCSS/DCS only filter chatter — they are not encryption. Other people on the channel can still hear you.
Hold the star (*) key for about 2 seconds to lock or unlock the keypad (side buttons still work). This radio also has 8 GMRS repeater channels for longer range.

This is a beginner overview, not a substitute for the official manual or FCC rules. Confirm current license fees at fcc.gov before you apply.

Like and follow for more how-tos.

snippet.title: FCC GMRS License & Beginner Rules Guide: Avoid Illegal Fines and Radio Mistakes
snippet.description:
Getting a General Mobile Radio Service (GMRS) license requires no technical exam, but transmitting up to 50 watts of UHF power comes with legal boundaries enforced by the Federal Communications Commission
. Because the FCC grants a 10-year license simply upon paying a $35 fee, thousands of new radio operators unintentionally violate federal rules, buy illegal equipment, and misconfigure repeaters on day one

In this documentary, we merge the complete FCC licensing walkthrough with a deep dive into 47 CFR Part 95 Subpart E regulations

You will learn how to navigate FCC CORES and ULS to secure your official call sign, who in your household is legally covered under a single fee, and how to avoid the critical technical traps surrounding power limits, privacy codes, and repeater offsets

snippet.title: Does a Dipole Antenna Have to Be Straight? (What Really Happens When You Bend It)
snippet.description:
Does a dipole antenna have to be perfectly straight to work properly? What happens if you bend the ends, slope the wires, or install it as an inverted V to fit your backyard?

In this video, Telecom Training explains how changing the shape of a dipole antenna affects its performance and what amateur-radio operators should know before installing one in a limited space.

We'll explore:

- Straight horizontal dipoles versus inverted-V antennas
- Bending dipole ends to fit smaller properties
- How antenna shape affects feed-point impedance and SWR
- Changes in radiation patterns and polarization
- The importance of antenna height and nearby objects
- Practical installation compromises for limited backyard space

A dipole doesn't always have to be straight. Understanding the trade-offs can help you make better use of the space you have.

Whether you're installing your first HF antenna or improving an existing setup, this video will help you understand what really matters.
